_comment: Screen-reader descriptions of what each chart shows. The visible caption already states the conclusion, so these describe the data instead of repeating it. Written from the rendered figures; keep in sync if a case regenerates its plots.
clinical_cohort_flow.png: Two-panel cohort diagram. Panel A, the clinical analysis population: 49 enrolled and treated across cohorts 5 and 6, splitting into cohort 5 with biopsiable disease (n=24) and cohort 6 without (n=25); these yield 18 of 36 planned and 21 of 35 planned RECIST-evaluable participants, with 6 partial responses each, combining to a response denominator of 39 of 49 and 12 partial responses. A note records that registry 'completed' n=43 is a disposition milestone, not the RECIST-evaluable n=39. Panel B, the pretreatment biopsy population: 24 baseline biopsies, of which 18 are tissue-quality eligible after 6 fail for high necrotic content; from these, 18 are DNA sequenced and 17 RNA sequenced, and 15 enter the post-hoc transcriptomic analysis after 2 exclusions, splitting into 6 participants with PFS at or beyond 6 months and 9 below.
replication_signal_robustness.png: Forest plot of seven DNA-replication score definitions, each showing a Hedges g effect estimate with a 95 percent stratified percentile-bootstrap confidence interval, plotted against a vertical line at zero effect. KEGG DNA replication mean z, p=0.234; Reactome HGNC-reconciled mean z, p=0.586; Reactome reconciled median z, p=0.608; Reactome reconciled ranks, p=0.583; Reactome DNA strand elongation, p=0.27; Reactome pre-replicative complex, p=0.199; Reactome exact-symbol only, p=0.591. Every one of the seven confidence intervals crosses zero.
mechanism_evidence_chain.png: Four bar panels of relative growth, each comparing control, siPOLA1, prexasertib, and the combination, with three replicate points per bar and an open diamond marking the descriptive Bliss-independence expectation. Panels cover two parental HGSOC lineages, OVCAR3 and OVCAR5, and their acquired prexasertib-resistant derivatives, OVCAR3-PrexR and OVCAR5-PrexR. In every panel the combination bar falls below the Bliss reference diamond. Footnotes record an unresolved dose-label conflict between the article prose, the figure caption, and the source-sheet title.
prexasertib_exposure_boundary.png: Scatter plot of geometric mean AUC from 0 to 72 hours, in nanogram-hours per millilitre, at four dose-by-cycle points from an external phase-1 study: 80 mg/m squared cycle 1 day 1 at 1,670 (n=6; CV 22 percent) and cycle 2 day 1 at 1,780 (n=4; CV 16 percent), then 105 mg/m squared cycle 1 day 1 at 2,160 (n=6; CV 13 percent) and cycle 2 day 1 at 2,270 (n=3; CV 22 percent). A dashed horizontal line marks a Calu-6 xenograft model target of 1,896. Both 105 mg/m squared points sit above that line and both 80 mg/m squared points below it. A side panel lists what the data can answer — regimen and external aggregate PK, and group dispersion as reported CV percent — and what it cannot: ovarian-trial participant PK, PK linked to response or PFS, and tumour exposure or target engagement.
clinical_safety_burden.png: Bar chart of grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events among 49 treated participants, each bar carrying a computed Wilson 95 percent confidence interval: neutropenia 42 participants (85.7 percent), leukocytopenia 38 (77.6 percent), thrombocytopenia 20 (40.8 percent), anemia 15 (30.6 percent), and febrile neutropenia 6 (12.2 percent). Accompanying counts record 11 participants (22.4 percent) with a toxicity-related dose reduction, 3 (6.1 percent) discontinuing for toxicity, and no on-treatment deaths.
